messages.content:
Let \( ABC \) be an isosceles triangle with \( AB = AC \). Points \( P \) and \( Q \) are located inside triangle \( ABC \) such that \( BP = PQ = QC \). Suppose that \( \angle BAP = 20^\circ \), \( \angle PAQ = 46^\circ \), and \( \angle QAC = 26^\circ \). Compute the measure of \( \angle APC \) in degrees.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let all angles be in degrees. Let the common length be  
\[
BP=PQ=QC=s.
\]

Since \(P,Q\) lie inside \(\triangle ABC\),
\[
\angle BAC=20^\circ+46^\circ+26^\circ=92^\circ.
\]
Because \(AB=AC\), the base angles are
\[
\angle ABC=\angle ACB=\frac{180^\circ-92^\circ}{2}=44^\circ.
\]

Let
\[
x=\angle APC.
\]
In \(\triangle APC\),
\[
\angle PAC=\angle PAQ+\angle QAC=46^\circ+26^\circ=72^\circ,
\]
so
\[
\angle ACP=180^\circ-72^\circ-x=108^\circ-x.
\]
Since \(P\) is inside the triangle, \(\angle ACP<44^\circ\), so \(x>64^\circ\).

Set
\[
\theta=x-54^\circ.
\]
Then
\[
x=54^\circ+\theta,\qquad \angle ACP=54^\circ-\theta,
\]
and the interior condition gives
\[
10^\circ<\theta<54^\circ.
\]

Let
\[
t=\angle QPC=\angle PCQ
\]
because \(PQ=QC\). In isosceles triangle \(PQC\), the base length is
\[
PC=2s\cos t.
\]

By the sine rule in \(\triangle APC\),
\[
AP=\frac{PC\sin\angle ACP}{\sin72^\circ}
   =\frac{2s\cos t\sin(54^\circ-\theta)}{\sin72^\circ},
\]
\[
AC=\frac{PC\sin x}{\sin72^\circ}
   =\frac{2s\cos t\sin(54^\circ+\theta)}{\sin72^\circ}.
\]

Since \(AB=AC\), we have \(AB=AC\). Applying the cosine law in \(\triangle ABP\), where \(\angle BAP=20^\circ\) and \(BP=s\),
\[
s^2=AP^2+AB^2-2(AP)(AB)\cos20^\circ.
\]
Substituting the expressions for \(AP\) and \(AB=AC\) and simplifying gives
\[
1=\frac{4M\cos^2 t}{\sin^2 72^\circ},
\]
where
\[
M=1-\cos20^\circ\cos72^\circ+(\cos72^\circ-\cos20^\circ)\cos2\theta.
\]

Now use the common side \(AQ\). In \(\triangle APQ\),
\[
\angle APQ=x+t=54^\circ+\theta+t,
\]
so
\[
AQ=\frac{s\sin(54^\circ+\theta+t)}{\sin46^\circ}.
\]
In \(\triangle AQC\),
\[
\angle ACQ=\angle ACP+t=54^\circ-\theta+t,
\]
so
\[
AQ=\frac{s\sin(54^\circ-\theta+t)}{\sin26^\circ}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{\sin(54^\circ+\theta+t)}{\sin46^\circ}
=
\frac{\sin(54^\circ-\theta+t)}{\sin26^\circ}.
\]
Let
\[
K=\frac{\sin46^\circ}{\sin26^\circ}.
\]
This gives
\[
\sin(54^\circ+\theta+t)=K\sin(54^\circ-\theta+t).
\]
Expanding and solving for \(\cos^2 t\) yields
\[
\cos^2 t=
\frac{\left(K\cos(54^\circ-\theta)-\cos(54^\circ+\theta)\right)^2}
{1+K^2-2K\cos2\theta}.
\]

Now simplify the numerator:
\[
\begin{aligned}
K\cos(54^\circ-\theta)-\cos(54^\circ+\theta)
&=\frac{\sin46^\circ\cos(54^\circ-\theta)-\sin26^\circ\cos(54^\circ+\theta)}{\sin26^\circ}\\
&=\frac{\cos18^\circ\sin(\theta+10^\circ)}{\sin26^\circ}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Also,
\[
1+K^2-2K\cos2\theta
=
\frac{M}{\sin^2 26^\circ}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\cos^2 t=\frac{\cos^2 18^\circ\sin^2(\theta+10^\circ)}{M}.
\]

Substitute this into
\[
1=\frac{4M\cos^2 t}{\sin^2 72^\circ}:
\]
\[
1=\frac{4\cos^2 18^\circ\sin^2(\theta+10^\circ)}{\sin^2 72^\circ}.
\]
Since \(\sin72^\circ=\cos18^\circ\),
\[
\sin(\theta+10^\circ)=\frac12.
\]
Because \(10^\circ<\theta<54^\circ\), we have \(20^\circ<\theta+10^\circ<64^\circ\), so the only solution is
\[
\theta+10^\circ=30^\circ.
\]
Hence
\[
\theta=20^\circ.
\]
Finally,
\[
\angle APC=x=54^\circ+\theta=54^\circ+20^\circ=74^\circ.
\]

\[
\boxed{74}
\]
